summary: Alabama taxes interest on other states' bonds even though that interest is federally tax-exempt. It exempts only interest on U.S. obligations and on Alabama or Alabama local obligations, plus Social Security. The prompt does not say the bonds are Alabama obligations, and it tells models to treat unlisted facts as false, so the $4,734 is Alabama AGI. Subtracting the $3,000 single standard deduction (AGI under $26,000) and the $1,500 personal exemption leaves $234, taxed at 2% = $4.68. The engine took the same path. It also built an itemized medical figure from about $2,585 of medical costs, apparently an imputed Medicare Part B premium plus the $150. That figure plus the employee business expense deduction is still below $3,000, so the standard deduction applies and the result is unchanged. The 0 consensus rests on the mistaken idea that Alabama exempts all federally tax-exempt interest, or on overstated deductions (Alabama has no extra 65+ standard deduction).
